text_blocks.snippet: Elevated PSA (prostate-specific antigen) levels can be a sign of prostate issues, including prostate cancer, but they can also be caused by other conditions like benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) (enlarged prostate) or prostatitis (inflammation or infection of the prostate). While high PSA levels themselves don't cause noticeable symptoms, the underlying conditions that cause elevated PSA can lead to urinary problems.
Symptoms of prostate conditions that can cause elevated PSA:

list.title: Urinary problems:
list.snippet: These can include frequent urination (especially at night), difficulty starting or stopping urination, weak urine stream, a feeling of incomplete bladder emptying, and painful or burning urination.
